 Nepal is pursuing a top-six finish in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 standings against host nation Oman at Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman on Monday, October 19, 2026. According to Nepal News, victory would secure Nepal's one-day international status directly, while failure to win would leave the team facing the World Cup Qualifier Playoffs. Live scorecard information published by India Today showed Nepal at 99 for three after 25.1 overs, with Dipendra Singh Airee and Rohit Paudel batting at the crease.
 Nepal won the toss and elected to bat in Match 139 of the 2023-27 competition. Nepal entered the decisive fixture in seventh place after losing to Canada by 24 runs in its previous match, according to Nepal News. Canada occupied sixth place, but Nepal's superior net run rate offered another potential route into the top six if the match against Oman were abandoned and Nepal received one point.

 The result carries significant consequences for Nepal's international status. A victory would allow the team to retain its ODI standing without entering the qualification playoffs, whereas a failure to win would force it to pursue that status through the additional tournament.

 Nepal Targets Top Six Finish to Retain ODI Status 
 Nepal had already demonstrated its ability to defeat Oman during the series, winning their second meeting by 113 runs, according to Nepal News. The team entered the latest contest seeking another victory against the host nation. The historical record between the teams was evenly balanced before the match. Nepal and Oman had played 12 one-day international matches against each other, with each side recording six wins, while Nepal had won their three most recent encounters, according to Nepal News.
 India Today's match information listed the venue as Al Amerat Cricket Ground Oman Cricket (Ministry Turf 1). Masudur Rahman of Bangladesh and Vinod Babu of Oman were the on-field umpires, while Wendell Labrooy of Sri Lanka served as match referee. Nepal's squad included Dev Khanal, Aasif Sheikh, Ishan Pandey, Rohit Paudel, Basir Ahamad, Dipendra Singh Airee, Gulshan Jha, Karan KC, Nandan Yadav, Sandeep Lamichhane and Lalit Rajbanshi. Sandeep Lamichhane was listed as captain, with Aasif Sheikh designated as wicketkeeper.
 Oman's squad featured Jatinder Singh, Hasnain Ul Wahab, Hammad Mirza, Mujibur Ali, Vinayak Shukla, Sanju Sajeev, Jay Odedra, Shah Faisal, Hassnain Shah, Shakeel Ahmed and Samay Shrivastava. Vinayak Shukla was listed as captain and wicketkeeper in the match information.
